explain.say: Let us sort! See the two groups light up. Rain this morning, windy today and a storm tonight are weather, because they are happening now. Hot every summer, dry all year and snowy winters are climate, because they happen year after year. Can you think of one more for each group?

Here is a trick: weather is your mood today, and climate is your personality. Well done! Wow fact: one snowy day did not change the Sahara’s climate. It is still one of the hottest, driest places on Earth.

faq.a: Weather is what the air is like at one place and time: how hot or cold it is, and whether it is rainy, windy, cloudy or sunny. It can change from hour to hour.
Climate is the usual weather of a place over a long time, usually worked out as an average over 30 years. For example, Egypt has a hot, dry climate.

faq.q: What is the difference between weather and climate?
faq.a: The difference is time. Weather is what happens today or this week; climate is the pattern over many years. People say: climate is what you expect, weather is what you get.
asks: Is weather the same as climate?

faq.q: Can it snow in the desert?
faq.a: Yes. Deserts get very little rain, but they can be cold at night and in winter. Snow fell near Aïn Séfra in Algeria, on the edge of the Sahara, in January 2018.
asks: Did it snow in the Sahara?

faq.q: Why do scientists use 30 years for climate?
faq.a: Thirty years is long enough to smooth out unusual years, so one very hot summer or one snowy winter does not change the average much.
asks: How long does it take to measure climate?

facts: Climate is usually worked out as an average of 30 years of weather.
